This is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) document.

## Text formatting

### Headings

```
## Level 2 heading
### Level 3 heading
#### Level 4 heading
##### Level 5 heading
###### Level 6 heading
```

### Character sizes

Custom text sizes are provided by this template.

|Markdown|Rendered|
|---|---|
|`[Largest text]{.largest}`|[Largest text]{.largest}|
|`[Larger text]{.larger}`|[Larger text]{.larger}|
|`[Large text]{.large}`|[Large text]{.large}|
|Normal text |Normal text|
|`[Small text]{.small}`|[Small text]{.small}|
|`[Smaller text]{.smaller}`|[Smaller text]{.smaller}|
|`[Smallest text]{.smallest}`|[Smallest text]{.smallest}|

### Character styles

|Markdown|Rendered|
|---|---|
|`__Bold text__`|__Bold text__|
|`_Italic text_`|_Italic text_|
|`~~Strikethrough~~`|~~Strikethrough~~|
|`H~2~O`|H~2~O|
|`x^2^`|x^2^|
|`--`|--|
|`---`|---|
|`[link](https://example.com/)`|[link](https://example.com/)|
|`{{{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P >}}}`|{{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P >}}|

### Blockquote

```
> This is a block quote. This
> paragraph has two lines.
>
> 1. This is a list inside a block quote.
> 2. Second item.
```

> This is a block quote. This paragraph has two lines.
>
> 1.  This is a list inside a block quote.
> 2.  Second item.

### Line block

A line block preserves spaces and line breaks.

```
| This
|     block
|          preserves
|                   formatting
```

| This
|     block
|          preserves
|                   formatting

### Rule

A horizontal line can be created using three or more `*` or `-`.

`***`

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Code formatting

Verbatim code is text formatted in a monospaced font and intended to be read as code. Inline verbatim code is enclosed in backticks, so `` `date()` `` renders as `date()`.

Verbatim code can also be placed in fenced code blocks.

````
```
date()
```
````

```
date()
```

Source code, that is, code that is syntax-highlighted or executed in a Quarto document, is not covered here in this document.

## Images

Images can be inserted using Markdown or HTML. In Markdown, Quarto attributes can control image properties. With the project's `lightbox: auto` setting, clicking an image opens it in a lightbox.

### Using Markdown

Using regular Markdown.

```
![](assets/image.webp)
```

![](assets/image.webp)

By default, an image uses its actual size, constrained by the available width. You can change its displayed dimensions as shown below.

```
![This is a caption](assets/image.webp){width=30%}
```

![This is a caption](assets/image.webp){width="30%"}

This image is now 30% of the available width.

#### Figure layout

```
::: {#fig-mylabel layout-ncol=2}
![Caption for figure 1](assets/image.webp){width="40%"}

![Caption for figure 2](assets/image.webp){width="40%"}

These figures are interesting.
:::
```

::: {#fig-mylabel layout-ncol="2"}
![Caption for figure 1](assets/image.webp){width="40%"}

![Caption for figure 2](assets/image.webp){width="40%"}

These figures are interesting.
:::

More figure options and layouts are described [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html). Cross-referencing is described [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/cross-references.html).

Here are some [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.0/utilities/shadows/) styles:

`![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow-sm rounded"}`

![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow-sm rounded"}

`![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow rounded"}`

![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow rounded"}

`![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow-lg rounded-pill"}`

![](assets/image.webp){width="20%" class="shadow-lg rounded-pill"}

### Using HTML

The image below is displayed at 30% width.\
`<img src="assets/image.webp" alt="Wooden dock overlooking a lake" style="width:30%;"/>`

<img src="assets/image.webp" alt="Wooden dock overlooking a lake" style="width:30%;"/>

For more information on figures, see [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html). Images generated through code are not covered here.

## Tables


For simple cases, tables can be manually created in Markdown.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-7}

```
|speed|dist|
|-----|----|
|4    |   2|
|4    |  10|
|7    |   4|
```

:::
::: {.g-col-5}

| speed | dist |
|-------|------|
| 4     | 2    |
| 4     | 10   |
| 7     | 4    |

:::
:::

Table captions and numbering can be added as follows:

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-7}

```
|speed|dist|
|-----|----|
|4    |   2|
|4    |  10|
|7    |   4|

: These are exciting results. {#tbl-mylabel}
```

:::
::: {.g-col-5}

| speed | dist |
|-------|------|
| 4     | 2    |
| 4     | 10   |
| 7     | 4    |

: These are exciting results. {#tbl-mylabel}

:::
:::

Tables can also be generated through code, which is not covered here.

### Margin table

A table placed in the margin.

```
::: {.column-margin}

| speed | dist |
|-------|------|
| 4     | 2    |
| 4     | 10   |
| 7     | 4    |

:::
```

::: {.column-margin}

| speed | dist |
|-------|------|
| 4     | 2    |
| 4     | 10   |
| 7     | 4    |

:::

See the [tables documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/tables.html) for more information.

### Cross-referencing

Figures and tables can be numbered by adding an identifier beginning with `fig-` or `tbl-`, such as `{#tbl-mylabel}`. Reference it with `@tbl-mylabel`, which renders as @tbl-mylabel.

## Icons

### Bootstrap Icons

[Bootstrap Icons](https://icons.getbootstrap.com) are available in Quarto HTML documents that use a Bootstrap-based theme. The Quarto [bsicons](https://github.com/shafayetShafee/bsicons) extension provides a shortcode interface.


`<i class="bi bi-lightbulb-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-lightbulb-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-clipboard2-check-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-clipboard2-check-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-chat-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-chat-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-laptop-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-laptop-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-cloud-fill"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-cloud-fill"></i>  
`<i class="bi bi-github"></i>`  <i class="bi bi-github"></i>  

### Font Awesome

To use [Font Awesome](https://fontawesome.com/search?m=free) icons with shortcodes, install the Quarto [fontawesome extension](https://github.com/quarto-ext/fontawesome).

Icons can be placed using shortcodes.

`{{{< fa lightbulb >}}}`      {{< fa lightbulb >}}  
`{{{< fa exclamation >}}}`    {{< fa exclamation >}}  
`{{{< fa clipboard-list >}}}` {{< fa clipboard-list >}}  
`{{{< fa comments >}}}`       {{< fa comments >}}  
`{{{< fa desktop >}}}`        {{< fa desktop >}}  
`{{{< fa cloud >}}}`          {{< fa cloud >}}  
`{{{< fa check >}}}`          {{< fa check >}}  
`{{{< fa times >}}}`          {{< fa times >}}  
`{{{< fa skull >}}}`          {{< fa skull >}}  
`{{{< fa skull size=2x >}}}`  {{< fa skull size=2x >}}  
`{{{< fa brands github >}}}`  {{< fa brands github >}}  
`{{{< fa brands youtube >}}}`  {{< fa brands youtube >}}  

Icons can be displayed using the HTML `<i>` tag. Note that not all icons may work.

`Here is a <i class="fa fa-calendar"></i> calendar and a <i class="fa fa-couch"></i> couch.`

Here is a <i class="fa fa-calendar"></i> calendar and a <i class="fa fa-couch"></i> couch.

There are many other Quarto extensions for icons, such as [academicons](https://github.com/schochastics/academicons), [iconify](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-iconify), and [lordicons](https://github.com/jmgirard/lordicon).

For a full list of icons, see [Font Awesome](https://fontawesome.com/search?m=free).

## Callouts

[Callout blocks](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/callouts.html) draw attention to specific information. Quarto provides five types: note, tip, caution, warning, and important.

```
::: {.callout-note}
Use notes for supplementary context that does not require the reader to take action. This should be the default for most things.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Use tips for optional advice that can make a task easier or more efficient.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
Use cautions when an action could have unwanted consequences that the reader should consider first.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Use warnings for actions that could cause mistakes, data loss, or other significant problems.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Use important callouts for essential information the reader must understand before continuing.
:::
```

::: {.callout-note}
Use notes for supplementary context that does not require the reader to take action. This should be the default for most things.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Use tips for optional advice that can make a task easier or more efficient.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
Use cautions when an action could have unwanted consequences that the reader should consider first.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Use warnings for actions that could cause mistakes, data loss, or other significant problems.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Use important callouts for essential information the reader must understand before continuing.
:::

Callout variations.

```
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Collapsible callout

This content is inside a collapsible callout.
:::
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Collapsible callout

This content is inside a collapsible callout.
:::

Simple appearance

```
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This is a callout with a simple appearance.
:::
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This is a callout with a simple appearance.
:::

Minimal appearance

This is a callout with a minimal appearance.

## Layout

### Span

`[Content inside span]{style="background-color: gray"}`

[Content inside span]{style="background-color: gray"}

### Div

```
::: {style="background-color: gray"}
Content inside div
:::
```

::: {style="background-color: gray"}
Content inside div
:::

Divs can be nested like this:

```
:::: {.class}
::: {.class}
:::
::::
```

Both spans and divs support attributes in this specific order: identifiers, classes, and then key-value attributes.

`[Content inside span]{#id .class key1="val1" key2="val2"}`

### Hidden div

```
::: {.hidden}
Hidden content
:::
```

### Conditional content

````
::: {{.content-visible when-format="html"}}
Will only appear in HTML.
:::
````

````
::: {{.content-hidden when-format="html"}}
Will not appear in HTML.
:::
````

Conditional content is documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/conditional.html).

More layout settings are described [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/article-layout.html) and [here](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/page-layout.html).

## Shortcodes

Quarto shortcodes are special Markdown directives that generate content.

The `meta` shortcode prints values from document metadata, including metadata inherited from `_quarto.yml`. Here are a few examples:

`{{{< meta title >}}}` {{< meta title >}}

`{{{< meta description >}}}` {{< meta description >}}

The `var` shortcode prints values from `_variables.yml`, `include` inserts another `.qmd` file, and `kbd` renders keyboard shortcuts:

`Press {{{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P >}}}` Press {{< kbd Shift-Ctrl-P >}}

The `video` shortcode embeds a video.

`{{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_f3latmOhew >}}}`

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_f3latmOhew >}}

The custom Lua filter adds the following metadata values, which can be read with the built-in `meta` shortcode:

`{{{< meta quarto_version >}}}` {{< meta quarto_version >}}  
`{{{< meta current_date >}}}` {{< meta current_date >}}  
`{{{< meta current_year >}}}` {{< meta current_year >}}  
`{{{< meta current_time >}}}` {{< meta current_time >}}  
`{{{< meta output-dir >}}}` {{< meta output-dir >}}  
`{{{< meta output-dir-path >}}}` {{< meta output-dir-path >}}  

The filter also exposes supported values from the **website**, **project**, and **format** blocks of `_quarto.yml` through the **custom.** prefix.

`{{{< meta custom.website.site-url >}}}` {{< meta custom.website.site-url >}}  
`{{{< meta custom.project.type >}}}` {{< meta custom.project.type >}}  
`{{{< meta custom.format.html.quarto-required >}}}` {{< meta custom.format.html.quarto-required >}}  

Shortcodes are documented [here](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/shortcodes.html).

## Accordions

Accordion support is provided through the [accordion](https://github.com/royfrancis/accordion) extension.

Accordion contents can be defined in the YAML front matter as shown below.

```yaml
accordion:
  - ac-1:
    - header: "**This is a header**"
      body: "This is **bold** and *italic* text"
```

and then rendered in the document body using the shortcode.

```markdown
{{{< accordion ac-1 >}}}
```

{{< accordion ac-1 >}}

Alternatively, an accordion can be defined inline as shown below.

```markdown
{{{< accordion label="my-accordion" header="Click to expand" body="This is the content of the accordion." >}}}
```

{{< accordion label="my-accordion" header="Click to expand" body="This is the content of the accordion." >}}

Multiple inline items can be defined using JSON.

```markdown
{{{< accordion label="inline-multi" items='[
  { "header": "Inline Item 1", "body": "Content for inline item 1." },
  { "header": "Inline Item 2", "body": "Content for inline item 2." }
]' >}}}
```

{{< accordion label="inline-multi" items='[
  { "header": "Inline Item 1", "body": "Content for inline item 1." },
  { "header": "Inline Item 2", "body": "Content for inline item 2." }
]' >}}

## Leaflet maps

Leaflet maps are enabled through the `leaflet` extension. Add map configuration to the page's YAML front matter or `_metadata.yml`, then use the `{{< leaflet mapname >}}` shortcode. See the [extension documentation](https://github.com/royfrancis/quarto-leaflet) for details.

```yaml
---
leaflet:
  zoom: 15
  ucl:
    markers:
      - tooltip: Venue
        icon: "fa-solid fa-briefcase"
        icon-color: "#E74856"
        lat: 51.5218
        lon: -0.1318
        popup: "Room 309<br> Roberts Building<br> University College London<br> Torrington Place<br> London WC1E 7JE<br> United Kingdom"
      - tooltip: "The Academy Hotel (0.2 km, 3 min walk)"
        icon: "fa-solid fa-bed"
        icon-color: "#0078D7"
        lat: 51.5244
        lon: -0.1328
        popup: "21 Gower Street<br> London WC1E 6HG<br> United Kingdom"
---

{{{< leaflet ucl >}}}
```

{{< leaflet ucl >}}

## General tips

-   Use level-2 headings (`##`) as the highest heading level:

  ```markdown
  ## Section A
  ```

-   Add a custom stylesheet in the YAML front matter if needed:

    ```yaml
    format:
      html:
        css: my-theme.css
    ```
-   See the [Quarto documentation](https://quarto.org/)
